# Purpose

This notebook draws Figure 1 of the Study 1 main text and writes the LaTeX
macros that the manuscript reads with `\input{}`. A macro is a short name,
such as `\SoneN`, that LaTeX replaces with its value when the manuscript is
compiled.

It fits no model and reruns no analysis. It reads:

  - `study1_long_with_text.csv`                        (the ratings, one row per participant, image and dimension)
  - `models/study1_lmm_creativity.rds`                 (the primary creativity model)
  - `models/study1_lmm_effort.rds`                     (the primary effort model)
  - `tables/study1_bootstrap_d.csv`                    (registered Cohen's d, the Human minus AI difference expressed in standard deviations, with an interval from resampling participants; written by Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv`            (the registered H1 contrasts, the Human minus AI difference on each dimension averaged over the two image kinds, checked against the F macros; written by Study1_01_Quant.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_effort_prevalence.csv`         (effort-talk rates, the share of effort justifications that mention each kind of reason; written by Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)
  - `tables/study1_text_creativity_prevalence.csv`     (creativity-talk rates, the same for creativity justifications; written by Study1_03_Integration.Rmd)

The last four are read only if they are on disk, so this notebook can be
knitted before the notebooks that write them have run. Each missing file has
its own consequence. Without the bootstrap table, d is computed here under the
same convention and the console says it is not the registered estimate.
Without the confirmatory family, the check of the F macros against it is
skipped. Without a prevalence table, its macros are left out. In each case the
console names the missing file.

It writes:

  - `figures/study1_fig1_ratings.{pdf,png}`  (Figure 1: the two rating dimensions, side by side)
  - `tables/study1_inline.tex`               (the LaTeX macro definitions; no other notebook writes this file)
  - `tables/study1_figures_run_manifest.csv` (the run record of the knit: every file read and written, with its fingerprint and status)

Every output is deleted before it is drawn or written, so a knit that stops
partway leaves no figure or macro file from an earlier knit behind.

The figures drawn from the written justifications come from
`Study1_03_Integration.Rmd`, where the text measures are joined to the ratings
and modelled. They show how often each kind of reason appears, detail talk
against the effort rating, and the denotation profiles, which set out what the
justifications under each rated word were about.

Knit again whenever the figure or the macros need refreshing. No model is
refit, so a knit is quick.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Project paths

The paths follow the same layout as `Study1_01_Quant.Rmd`, and `PROJECT_ROOT`
is found the same way: from this file's own folder, or from the environment
variable `STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT` when it is set.

```{r paths}
PROJECT_ROOT <- local({
  is_root <- function(p) dir.exists(file.path(p, "Data")) &&
                         dir.exists(file.path(p, "Analysis"))
  root <- Sys.getenv("STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT")
  if (nzchar(root)) {
    root <- normalizePath(root, mustWork = FALSE)
    if (!is_root(root)) {
      stop("The folder STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT names has no Data and Analysis ",
           "folders.")
    }
  } else {
    root <- normalizePath(getwd(), mustWork = TRUE)
    while (!is_root(root)) {
      if (identical(dirname(root), root)) {
        stop("No folder at or above the working directory holds both Data ",
             "and Analysis. Knit this file from its own folder, or set ",
             "STUDY1_PROJECT_ROOT to the project root.")
      }
      root <- dirname(root)
    }
  }
  root
})

STUDY_NUM    <- 1
STUDY_FOLDER <- paste("Study", STUDY_NUM)

PATH_ANALYSIS    <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "Analysis",
                              "R Analysis Pipeline", STUDY_FOLDER)
PATH_OUT         <- PATH_ANALYSIS
PATH_OUT_FIG     <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "figures")
PATH_OUT_TAB     <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "tables")
PATH_OUT_MODELS  <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "models")

PATH_PAPER       <- file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "Docs", "Writing", "Final Paper")
PATH_PAPER_FIG   <- file.path(PATH_PAPER, "figures")
PATH_PAPER_TAB   <- file.path(PATH_PAPER, "tables")

# The run record of this knit sits beside the analysis tables, under the name
# every stage of the pipeline uses: tables/study1_<stage>_run_manifest.csv.
PATH_RUN_MANIFEST <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_figures_run_manifest.csv")

# Stop at once if the project folder cannot be found.
if (!dir.exists(PROJECT_ROOT)) {
  stop("PROJECT_ROOT does not exist:\n  ", PROJECT_ROOT,
       "\nIs Google Drive mounted? Edit PROJECT_ROOT to point to your copy.")
}

# Create the output folders if they are missing.
for (p in c(PATH_OUT_FIG, PATH_OUT_TAB,
            PATH_PAPER_FIG, PATH_PAPER_TAB)) {
  dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

cat("Figures will be written to:\n  ", PATH_OUT_FIG,
    "\n   and\n  ", PATH_PAPER_FIG, "\n")
```

## 1.3 Run record

Each knit has a run identifier and keeps a list of the files it read and
wrote. The last chunk saves that list to `tables/study1_figures_run_manifest.csv`.

```{r run-record}
# One row per file: the run identifier, the stage, the role of the file (this
# source file, an input or an output), its path within the project, its
# SHA-256 fingerprint (a 64-character code computed from the file's bytes,
# which changes if a single byte changes), its size, and a status (knitted,
# read, absent or written) with a note. The manifest from an earlier knit is
# deleted here, before anything else is written, so a knit that stops partway
# leaves no manifest claiming it finished. The digest package computes the
# fingerprints; it is called as digest::digest() and is not attached with
# library().
RUN_STAGE   <- "figures"
RUN_STARTED <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")
RUN_ID      <- paste0(RUN_STAGE, "-", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"), "-",
                      substr(digest::digest(c(RUN_STARTED, Sys.getpid())), 1, 8))
unlink(PATH_RUN_MANIFEST)

# The file being knitted. When the code runs outside a knit, the copy in the
# analysis folder is fingerprinted instead.
SOURCE_FILE <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
if (is.null(SOURCE_FILE)) {
  SOURCE_FILE <- file.path(PATH_ANALYSIS, "Study1_Figures.Rmd")
}

file_sha256 <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NA_character_)
  digest::digest(file = path, algo = "sha256")
}
path_in_project <- function(path) {
  root <- paste0(PROJECT_ROOT, "/")
  ifelse(startsWith(path, root), substring(path, nchar(root) + 1L), path)
}

# The fingerprint and size are taken from the full path before the row is
# built. Inside tibble() a later argument can see an earlier column, and the
# path column there holds the project-relative form, not the full path.
run_ledger <- list()
record_file <- function(role, path, status, note = "") {
  sha   <- file_sha256(path)
  bytes <- if (file.exists(path)) file.size(path) else NA_real_
  run_ledger[[length(run_ledger) + 1L]] <<- tibble::tibble(
    run_id = RUN_ID, stage = RUN_STAGE, role = role,
    path   = path_in_project(path), status = status,
    sha256 = sha, bytes = bytes, note = note
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}
record_file("source", SOURCE_FILE, "knitted")
```

## 1.4 Theme and palette

Figure 1 uses one greyscale palette and one `theme_paper()` function for its
axes and panel labels. Grey prints cleanly in black and white, and it gives
neither condition a colour that could read as a judgment about it.

```{r theme}
PAL_TYPE <- c("Human" = "#A1A1A1", "AI" = "#3E3E3E")

theme_paper <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "none",
      strip.background   = element_blank(),
      strip.placement    = "outside",
      strip.text         = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      axis.line          = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks         = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.text          = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid         = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold",
                                        hjust = 0),
      plot.margin        = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
    )
}
```

# 2. Load data

```{r load-data}
# The ratings from Study1_01_Quant.Rmd in long format: one row per
# participant, image and dimension.
long_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT, "study1_long_with_text.csv")
record_file("input", long_path, if (file.exists(long_path)) "read" else "absent")
long <- read_csv(long_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    Type          = factor(Type,          levels = c("Human", "AI")),
    stimulus_type = factor(stimulus_type, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure")),
    dimension     = factor(dimension,     levels = c("creativity", "effort")),
    id            = factor(id),
    stimulus_id   = factor(stimulus_id)
  )

# Checks on the structure. No identifier is missing. Each participant has one
# Type, the attribution condition (told that a person, Human, or AI made the
# works), and 10 ratings on each dimension, one per image: 5 figurative and 5
# non-figurative.
stopifnot(!any(is.na(long$id)), !any(is.na(long$Type)),
          !any(is.na(long$dimension)), !any(is.na(long$stimulus_id)))
stopifnot(all((long %>% distinct(id, Type) %>% count(id) %>% pull(n)) == 1L))
stopifnot(all((long %>% count(id, dimension) %>% pull(n)) == 10L))

cat("Ratings loaded: ", nrow(long), " rows, ",
    dplyr::n_distinct(long$id), " participants.\n", sep = "")
```

# 3. Figure 1: Ratings by Creator Type

Figure 1 has two panels, creativity on the left and effort on the right. Each
dot is one participant's mean rating over the ten images, both image kinds
together, so every participant appears once in each panel. Behind the dots, a
violin gives a smoothed outline of how those means are spread (wider where
more participants fall), and a boxplot marks the median and the middle half of
the participants.

```{r fig1-ratings, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=3.6}
# Both copies of the figure are deleted before it is drawn, so a knit that
# stops in this chunk leaves no figure from an earlier knit behind.
fig1_paths <- as.vector(outer(c(PATH_OUT_FIG, PATH_PAPER_FIG),
                              c("study1_fig1_ratings.pdf",
                                "study1_fig1_ratings.png"),
                              file.path))
unlink(fig1_paths)

participant_cell <- long %>%
  group_by(id, Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_mean = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    dimension = factor(stringr::str_to_title(as.character(dimension)),
                       levels = c("Creativity", "Effort"))
  )

# Jitter is a small random sideways shift that keeps overlapping dots
# visible. `height = 0` confines it to the category axis, so each dot stays at
# its true participant mean on the rating axis. The shift is drawn from a
# fixed seed (20260421), so every knit places each dot in the same spot.
# `coord_cartesian(ylim=)` narrows the view without removing data. Setting
# `scale_y_continuous(limits=)` instead would turn any value outside the
# limits into NA and drop it from the violin and boxplot as well, without a
# message.
fig1 <- ggplot(participant_cell,
               aes(x = Type, y = rating_mean, fill = Type)) +
  geom_violin(width = 0.85, alpha = 0.55, trim = FALSE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.22, alpha = 0.85, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(width = 0.07, height = 0,
                                         seed = 20260421),
              alpha = 0.30, size = 0.8, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_TYPE) +
  labs(x = "Creator Type", y = "Mean rating (1–5)") +
  theme_paper(base_size = 11)

fig1

# Save to both the analysis folder and the manuscript folder.
# 7.2 in is about 18.3 cm, the Nature Communications double-column width.
for (target_dir in c(PATH_OUT_FIG, PATH_PAPER_FIG)) {
  ggsave(file.path(target_dir, "study1_fig1_ratings.pdf"),
         fig1, width = 7.2, height = 3.6, device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(target_dir, "study1_fig1_ratings.png"),
         fig1, width = 7.2, height = 3.6, dpi = 300)
}
for (p in fig1_paths) record_file("output", p, "written")
```

# 4. Inline LaTeX macros

This section writes `study1_inline.tex`. It defines, as `\newcommand{}`
macros, each Study 1 number that this notebook supplies to the manuscript
text. The manuscript, kept on Overleaf (an online LaTeX editor), should load
the file near the top of the document with

```
\input{tables/study1_inline.tex}
```

and then use the macro names in place of numbers, for example
`\SoneMCreatHum` for the mean creativity rating in the Human condition. A
number typed by hand can drift from the analysis; a macro cannot, provided the
manuscript source does load this file.

**One writer per file.** This notebook is the only writer of
`study1_inline.tex`, and every macro in it starts with `\Sone` followed by a
CamelCase name. A notebook that needs macros of its own writes them to a file
of its own. If two notebooks wrote the same file, the one knitted last would
overwrite the other without warning.

```{r inline-stats}
# This chunk is the only writer of study1_inline.tex (see the text above). Do
# not add a second writer.

# Both copies of the macro file are deleted first, so a check that stops this
# chunk leaves no macro file from an earlier knit for the manuscript to read.
inline_paths <- file.path(c(PATH_OUT_TAB, PATH_PAPER_TAB), "study1_inline.tex")
unlink(inline_paths)

# The two primary models saved by Study1_01_Quant.Rmd. Each is a linear mixed
# model: a regression of the rating on attribution, image kind and their
# interaction that gives each participant and each image its own baseline.
creat_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity.rds")
eff_path   <- file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort.rds")
creat_res  <- readRDS(creat_path)
eff_res    <- readRDS(eff_path)
record_file("input", creat_path, "read")
record_file("input", eff_path,   "read")

# Formatting for an F test, a p-value, and a d with its interval.
fmt_F <- function(row) sprintf("$F(%.0f, %.1f) = %.2f$",
                               row$NumDF, row$DenDF, row$`F value`)
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p))      "NA"
  else if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001"
  else                sprintf("%.3f", p)
}
fmt_d <- function(d, lo, hi) sprintf("%.2f, 95\\%% CI [%.2f, %.2f]",
                                     d, lo, hi)

# The Type row of each model's ANOVA table, which tests each model term with
# an F statistic (denominator degrees of freedom by the Satterthwaite
# approximation).
ac <- as.data.frame(creat_res$anova_sat) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  filter(term == "Type")
ae <- as.data.frame(eff_res$anova_sat) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  filter(term == "Type")
stopifnot(nrow(ac) == 1L, nrow(ae) == 1L)

# What the Type F tests. Each dimension's primary model includes the
# attribution-by-image-kind interaction. In that model the type III F for
# Type (which tests Type after every other term is in the model) tests the
# attribution difference averaged with equal weight over the two image kinds.
# That average is the registered H1 contrast. It is not the TypeAI
# coefficient, which is the difference at the non-figurative image kind only.
# With one numerator degree of freedom (a single contrast under test), the F
# is the square of the contrast's t and has the same p-value. When the
# confirmatory family is on disk the two are compared here, and the chunk
# stops if they disagree, since that would mean the macro and the registered
# test came from different fits.
conf_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_confirmatory_family.csv")
if (file.exists(conf_path)) {
  conf_fam <- read_csv(conf_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  record_file("input", conf_path, "read")
  stopifnot(all(c("hypothesis", "test", "statistic", "p_raw") %in% names(conf_fam)))
  check_h1_F <- function(row, dim) {
    h1 <- conf_fam %>%
      filter(hypothesis == "H1", grepl(dim, test, ignore.case = TRUE))
    stopifnot(nrow(h1) == 1L, row$NumDF == 1)
    if (abs(row$`F value` - h1$statistic^2) > 1e-4 * max(1, h1$statistic^2) ||
        abs(row$`Pr(>F)` - h1$p_raw) > 1e-6 + 1e-4 * h1$p_raw) {
      stop(sprintf(paste0("The %s Type F (%.4f, p = %.3g) does not match the ",
                          "square of the registered H1 t (%.4f, p = %.3g) in ",
                          "study1_confirmatory_family.csv. Re-run ",
                          "Study1_01_Quant.Rmd so both come from one fit."),
                   dim, row$`F value`, row$`Pr(>F)`, h1$statistic^2, h1$p_raw))
    }
    cat(sprintf("%s: Type F = %.3f equals the registered H1 t squared (%.3f).\n",
                dim, row$`F value`, h1$statistic^2))
  }
  check_h1_F(ac, "creativity")
  check_h1_F(ae, "effort")
} else {
  cat("pending: run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 7.9 (missing ",
      "study1_confirmatory_family.csv); the Type F macros are written without ",
      "the check against the registered H1 contrast.\n", sep = "")
  record_file("input", conf_path, "absent")
}

# Sample sizes are counted from the data. Each participant id must belong to
# exactly one Type. The counts are then checked against the analytic N of 111
# (56 Human, 55 AI).
id_type <- long %>% distinct(id, Type)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(id_type$id)), !any(is.na(id_type$Type)))
n_total <- nrow(id_type)
n_hum   <- sum(id_type$Type == "Human")
n_ai    <- sum(id_type$Type == "AI")
stopifnot(n_total == n_hum + n_ai)
stopifnot(n_total == 111L, n_hum == 56L, n_ai == 55L)  # analytic N

# Cell means. Each participant's ratings are first averaged over all ten
# images, both image kinds together; the mean and SD of those participant
# means are then taken within each Type and dimension.
marg <- long %>%
  group_by(id, Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(m), SD = sd(m), N = n(), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(marg) == 4L)

pull1 <- function(df, col) {
  x <- df[[col]]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1L, !is.na(x))
  x
}
m_creat_hum <- marg %>% filter(Type == "Human", dimension == "creativity") %>% pull1("M")
m_creat_ai  <- marg %>% filter(Type == "AI",    dimension == "creativity") %>% pull1("M")
m_eff_hum   <- marg %>% filter(Type == "Human", dimension == "effort")     %>% pull1("M")
m_eff_ai    <- marg %>% filter(Type == "AI",    dimension == "effort")     %>% pull1("M")

sd_creat_hum <- marg %>% filter(Type == "Human", dimension == "creativity") %>% pull1("SD")
sd_creat_ai  <- marg %>% filter(Type == "AI",    dimension == "creativity") %>% pull1("SD")
sd_eff_hum   <- marg %>% filter(Type == "Human", dimension == "effort")     %>% pull1("SD")
sd_eff_ai    <- marg %>% filter(Type == "AI",    dimension == "effort")     %>% pull1("SD")

# ---- Cohen's d ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Cohen's d is the difference between two group means divided by their pooled
# SD (the spread of scores within the groups, combined across both groups
# with each weighted by its size). The registered convention
# (Docs/Preregistration/Study1_Preregistration.md, section 6) is
# d = (M_Human - M_AI) / pooled SD on participant means, with a bootstrap
# percentile CI: the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of d over B = 10,000
# resamples of participants, seed 20260421. Study1_01_Quant.Rmd saves the
# result to tables/study1_bootstrap_d.csv. This chunk reads that CSV, so the
# manuscript macro and the supplement table (Study1_Supplements.Rmd section
# 10.5) report the same numbers. If the CSV is absent, d is computed below
# under the same convention and the console says so. If it is present but
# lacks the expected columns, the chunk stops.
boot_path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_bootstrap_d.csv")
if (file.exists(boot_path)) {
  bd <- read_csv(boot_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  record_file("input", boot_path, "read")
  bd_req <- c("dimension", "d", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")
  if (!all(bd_req %in% names(bd))) {
    stop("study1_bootstrap_d.csv exists but lacks expected columns (",
         paste(bd_req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(bd), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align the writer in Study1_01_Quant.Rmd or this reader.")
  }
  # Sign convention: the CSV stores M_Human - M_AI, and the manuscript reports
  # the size of the gap, |Human - AI|, so abs() is applied here. Taking
  # absolute values is safe only when d and both CI limits have the same
  # sign. A CI that crosses zero would be folded into a positive interval that
  # misstates the uncertainty. The sign check therefore runs on the signed
  # values, before abs(), because after folding a crossing interval looks the
  # same as one that lies on one side of zero.
  get_d <- function(dim) {
    r <- bd %>% filter(dimension == dim)
    stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1L, !is.na(r$d), !is.na(r$ci_lo), !is.na(r$ci_hi),
              r$ci_lo <= r$d, r$d <= r$ci_hi)
    if (sign(r$ci_lo) != sign(r$ci_hi) || sign(r$d) != sign(r$ci_lo)) {
      stop(sprintf(paste0("study1_bootstrap_d.csv: %s CI [%.3f, %.3f] ",
                          "straddles zero; |Human - AI| cannot be reported ",
                          "from abs(). Report the signed d in the manuscript."),
                   dim, r$ci_lo, r$ci_hi))
    }
    list(d = abs(r$d), lo = min(abs(r$ci_lo), abs(r$ci_hi)),
         hi = max(abs(r$ci_lo), abs(r$ci_hi)))
  }
  d_creat <- get_d("creativity")
  d_eff   <- get_d("effort")
  stopifnot(d_creat$lo <= d_creat$hi, d_eff$lo <= d_eff$hi)
  bd_B    <- if ("B"    %in% names(bd)) as.integer(bd$B[1])    else NA_integer_
  bd_seed <- if ("seed" %in% names(bd)) as.integer(bd$seed[1]) else NA_integer_
  d_source <- sprintf("registered: tables/study1_bootstrap_d.csv (B = %s, seed = %s)",
                      ifelse(is.na(bd_B), "see Study1_01_Quant.Rmd", bd_B),
                      ifelse(is.na(bd_seed), "see Study1_01_Quant.Rmd", bd_seed))
  cat("Cohen's d read from", boot_path, "\n")
} else {
  # Fallback when the registered CSV is missing. d is computed here under the
  # registered convention: participant means, pooled SD, stratified resampling
  # of participants, percentile CI, B = 10,000, seed 20260421. These values
  # are not the registered numbers. The macros carry those only after
  # Study1_01_Quant.Rmd section 9.1 writes the CSV and this notebook is
  # knitted again.
  # Stratified means that each arm's participants are resampled separately,
  # so both arm sizes stay fixed across replicates. Study1_01_Quant.Rmd
  # resamples the same way. Resampling the two arms as one pool would let
  # their sizes vary and would not be the registered scheme.
  warning("tables/study1_bootstrap_d.csv not found; falling back to inline ",
          "bootstrap d. Run Study1_01_Quant.Rmd (registered bootstrap d) and ",
          "re-knit so the manuscript macros carry the registered estimate.")
  cat("Warning: study1_bootstrap_d.csv not found; d is computed inline ",
      "and is not the registered estimate.\n")
  record_file("input", boot_path, "absent", "inline bootstrap d used in its place")
  B <- 10000L
  pooled_d <- function(x_h, x_a) {
    n_h <- length(x_h); n_a <- length(x_a)
    sp  <- sqrt(((n_h - 1) * var(x_h) + (n_a - 1) * var(x_a)) / (n_h + n_a - 2))
    (mean(x_h) - mean(x_a)) / sp
  }
  boot_d <- function(dim_name) {
    pp <- long %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
      group_by(id, Type) %>% summarise(m = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
    h <- pp$m[pp$Type == "Human"]; a <- pp$m[pp$Type == "AI"]
    stopifnot(length(h) > 2L, length(a) > 2L)
    d_obs <- pooled_d(h, a)
    set.seed(20260421)   # reset per dimension, as in Quant section 9.1
    reps <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
      pooled_d(sample(h, length(h), replace = TRUE),
               sample(a, length(a), replace = TRUE))
    }, numeric(1))
    ci <- unname(quantile(reps, c(0.025, 0.975), type = 7))
    # Signed d and CI must share a sign for the |Human - AI| report.
    if (sign(ci[1]) != sign(ci[2]) || sign(d_obs) != sign(ci[1])) {
      stop(sprintf(paste0("Fallback bootstrap d for %s has a CI straddling ",
                          "zero [%.3f, %.3f]; report the signed d instead."),
                   dim_name, ci[1], ci[2]))
    }
    list(d = abs(d_obs), lo = min(abs(ci)), hi = max(abs(ci)))
  }
  d_creat <- boot_d("creativity")
  d_eff   <- boot_d("effort")
  d_source <- sprintf("fallback, inline bootstrap (B = %d, seed 20260421), not the registered CSV", B)
}

# ---- Text-measure rates for the manuscript's headline sentences --------------
# The written justifications are measured by fixed search patterns in
# Study1_02_Text.ipynb and modelled in Study1_03_Integration.Rmd, which writes
# the two prevalence tables read here. Both give one row per quantity with a
# participant-resampled 95% interval, one obtained by resampling whole
# participants so that each person's justifications stay together. The macros
# below report those numbers, rounded to whole percentages, and do not
# recompute them under a slightly different convention.
#
# Both rates are for the arm told a person made the work. That is the arm the
# denotation questions are about: what the words "effort" and "creativity"
# meant to someone judging a human-made picture. The machine arm's own use of
# the words is a separate question, reported in Study1_03_Integration.Rmd.
#
# Each read is guarded by file.exists(). If a table has not been written yet,
# its macros are left out and the console names the notebook section that
# writes it. A macro file with gaps is safer than one carrying numbers no
# analysis produced.
read_prevalence <- function(csv_name, section) {
  path <- file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, csv_name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    cat("pending: run Study1_03_Integration.Rmd ", section,
        " (missing ", csv_name, ")\n", sep = "")
    record_file("input", path, "absent")
    return(NULL)
  }
  d <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  record_file("input", path, "read")
  req <- c("quantity", "estimate", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")
  if (!all(req %in% names(d))) {
    stop(csv_name, " is missing expected columns (",
         paste(req, collapse = ", "), "). Found: ",
         paste(names(d), collapse = ", "),
         ". Align Study1_03_Integration.Rmd (writer) with this reader.")
  }
  d
}

prev_effort <- read_prevalence("study1_text_effort_prevalence.csv",
                               "section 3.1 (effort-talk prevalence)")
prev_creat  <- read_prevalence("study1_text_creativity_prevalence.csv",
                               "section 4.1 (creativity-talk prevalence)")

# One macro per quantity: the rate as a whole percentage, with the
# participant-resampled interval beside it in the same units.
prevalence_macro <- function(d, wanted, macro) {
  if (is.null(d)) return(character(0))
  r <- d[!is.na(d$quantity) & d$quantity == wanted, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(r) != 1L) {
    stop(sprintf(paste0("Expected exactly one row for the quantity '%s' but ",
                        "found %d. Quantities present: %s."),
                 wanted, nrow(r), paste(d$quantity, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (is.na(r$estimate) || is.na(r$ci_lo) || is.na(r$ci_hi)) {
    stop(sprintf("The row for '%s' has an NA estimate or interval.", wanted))
  }
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\%s}{%.0f\\%% (95\\%% CI [%.0f, %.0f])}",
          macro, 100 * r$estimate, 100 * r$ci_lo, 100 * r$ci_hi)
}

text_macros <- c(
  prevalence_macro(prev_effort, "detail",         "SoneEffortDetail"),
  prevalence_macro(prev_effort, "time",           "SoneEffortTime"),
  prevalence_macro(prev_effort, "skill",          "SoneEffortSkill"),
  prevalence_macro(prev_creat,  "concept",        "SoneCreatConcept"),
  prevalence_macro(prev_creat,  "novelty_either", "SoneCreatNovelty"),
  prevalence_macro(prev_creat,  "execution",      "SoneCreatExecution")
)

# The macro file, line by line.
lines <- c(
  "% Written by Study1_Figures.Rmd, the only writer of this file. Do not edit by hand.",
  "% Edit Study1_Figures.Rmd, knit, and re-input this file.",
  "% A notebook that needs macros of its own writes them to a file of its own.",
  "",
  "% --- Sample (derived from study1_long_with_text.csv) ---",
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneN}{%d}",    n_total),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneNHum}{%d}", n_hum),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneNAI}{%d}",  n_ai),
  "",
  "% --- H1: attribution effect on each dimension, averaged over the two image kinds",
  "% (type III F for Type in the primary model; the same test as the registered marginal contrast) ---",
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneCreatTypeF}{%s}",  fmt_F(ac)),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneCreatTypeP}{%s}",  fmt_p(ac$`Pr(>F)`)),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneEffTypeF}{%s}",    fmt_F(ae)),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneEffTypeP}{%s}",    fmt_p(ae$`Pr(>F)`)),
  "",
  "% --- Cell means ---",
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneMCreatHum}{%.2f}",  m_creat_hum),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneMCreatAI}{%.2f}",   m_creat_ai),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneMEffHum}{%.2f}",    m_eff_hum),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneMEffAI}{%.2f}",     m_eff_ai),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneSDCreatHum}{%.2f}", sd_creat_hum),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneSDCreatAI}{%.2f}",  sd_creat_ai),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneSDEffHum}{%.2f}",   sd_eff_hum),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneSDEffAI}{%.2f}",    sd_eff_ai),
  "",
  sprintf("%% --- Cohen's d (|Human - AI| on participant means; source: %s) ---", d_source),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneCreatD}{%s}", fmt_d(d_creat$d, d_creat$lo, d_creat$hi)),
  sprintf("\\newcommand{\\SoneEffD}{%s}",   fmt_d(d_eff$d,   d_eff$lo,   d_eff$hi)),
  ""
)

# The text-measure macros are appended only for the tables that exist. Their
# comment line is written with them, so a manuscript reading this file never
# finds a heading with nothing under it.
if (length(text_macros) > 0) {
  lines <- c(
    lines,
    paste0("% --- Rates in the written justifications, human-attribution arm ",
           "(share of justifications, with a participant-resampled 95% CI) ---"),
    text_macros,
    ""
  )
}

# Write the same file to the analysis tables folder and the manuscript tables
# folder.
for (p in inline_paths) {
  writeLines(lines, p)
  record_file("output", p, "written")
}

# Print the file in the knitted report.
cat(paste(lines, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

# 5. Output manifest

This notebook writes:

```
figures/
  study1_fig1_ratings.pdf      # Figure 1 (two panels of violins, creativity and effort)
  study1_fig1_ratings.png

tables/
  study1_inline.tex            # \newcommand{} macros for the manuscript text (only writer)
  study1_figures_run_manifest.csv  # run record of the knit (analysis folder only)
```

The figure and the macro file are written to both `Analysis/.../Study 1/`
and the `Final Paper/` folder, so the manuscript can read them from its own
folder without a copy step.

```{r run-manifest}
# The run record of this knit: one row per role and path, with the start and
# finish times and the R version beside each row. It is written last, after
# every other chunk has finished, so its presence means the knit ran to the
# end.
run_manifest <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_ledger) %>%
  group_by(role, path) %>%
  slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(started_at  = RUN_STARTED,
         finished_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
         r_version   = R.version.string) %>%
  arrange(factor(role, levels = c("source", "input", "output")), path)
write_csv(run_manifest, PATH_RUN_MANIFEST)
cat("Run ", RUN_ID, ": ",
    sum(run_manifest$role == "output" & run_manifest$status == "written"),
    " outputs written. Run record written to ", basename(PATH_RUN_MANIFEST),
    ".\n", sep = "")
run_manifest %>% count(role, status)
```

# 6. Notes

  - Every input is a saved analysis output, and no model is refit. A knit
    takes about 5 s, longer on the fallback path, which draws B = 10,000
    bootstrap resamples.
  - After rerunning an analysis notebook, knit this file again. To change
    Figure 1, edit its chunk in section 3 and knit again.
  - Figure 1 is 7.2 in wide (about 18.3 cm), the Nature Communications
    double-column width.
  - The figures built from the written justifications come from
    `Study1_03_Integration.Rmd`, beside the models they summarise. This
    notebook draws only Figure 1 and reads that notebook's prevalence tables
    for the macros in section 4.
  - Every macro in `study1_inline.tex` comes from a saved analysis output,
    except d on the fallback path, which is computed here. A text-measure
    quantity whose table is not on disk gets no macro, and the console names
    the section that writes the table.
  - The two Type F macros test the H1 contrast, the attribution difference
    averaged over the two image kinds. When
    `tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv` is on disk, the knit stops if
    either F differs from the square of the registered contrast's t.
  - The figure files and the macro file are deleted at the start of the chunk
    that writes them, and `tables/study1_figures_run_manifest.csv` records the
    fingerprint of every file the knit read and wrote.
